title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of an early ’69 Avalon show, spotlighting a blistering Clementine and Death Don't Have No Mercy with strong overall performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is a fresh, well‑transferred soundboard tape that most listeners describe as the best‑sounding version on the Archive, despite occasional early‑mix dips. Musically the concert shines in its second set – Clementine, The Eleven, Turn On Your Lovelight and Death Don't Have No Mercy are repeatedly called “pure gold,” while Dark Star and St. Stephen are seen as merely serviceable for the period.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4‑5) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and audio quality outweigh a few minor criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Fresh transfer praised as crisp and clean; a few reviewers note early mix issues or occasional dips, but overall the sound is clear, balanced, and among the best on the archive.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A compact, high‑energy set typical of the Avalon run; second set is especially praised for its psychedelic intensity and seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s bluesy lead on Death Don't and his raw, emotional vocal delivery are highlighted; some note a slightly labored feel on Clementine but overall strong playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work is praised, especially during the riff recap in the Clementine breakdown; his leadership in that section is noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) receives multiple accolades for trippy organ arpeggios and a prominent mix that adds depth to the psychedelic sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are described as “pounding” and driving the intensity upward throughout the night.
